# Meal Manager — full agent guide

This document tells an LLM client (or its operator) how to interact with a Meal Manager instance.

## What Meal Manager is

A self-hosted family app to manage:
- **Inventory** (pantry + fridge + freezer), with quantities in canonical units (`g`, `ml`, `unit`).
- **Recipes**, each with an ingredient list, servings, instructions.
- **Weekly menus** (breakfast/lunch/dinner × 7 days).
- **Shopping lists** derived from a menu (menu × servings − current inventory).
- **Ingredients catalog** (the master list referenced by inventory, recipes, shopping).

All data is scoped to a **household**. A user belongs to at most one household at a time, and can share it with other family members.

## Integration: MCP HTTP/SSE

Meal Manager exposes a **Model Context Protocol** server at `POST /mcp` (with `GET /mcp` and `DELETE /mcp` per the StreamableHTTP transport spec). Operates in stateless mode: each POST is self-contained.

### Authentication

Bearer Personal Access Token (PAT) in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer mm_pat_<22 base64url chars>
```

- Tokens are created from `/settings/tokens` in the web UI.
- Each token is **bound to a specific (user, household)** at issuance time and cannot be retargeted.
- The plaintext is shown **once** at creation. Only its SHA-256 hash is persisted. If lost, create a new one.
- Tokens are revocable from the same UI. Revocation takes effect immediately.

On any auth failure, the server responds `401 Unauthorized` with:
```
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="meal-manager-mcp"
```

OAuth 2.1 is on the roadmap — both schemes will coexist when added.

### Required request headers

Every MCP request MUST carry:

- `Authorization: Bearer <plaintext PAT>` — covered above.
- `Content-Type: application/json` — JSON-RPC payload.
- `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` — **both** media types, per the StreamableHTTP transport spec. A request that accepts only one will be rejected with HTTP 406 ("Not Acceptable: Client must accept both application/json and text/event-stream"). Real MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Home Assistant) set this automatically — you only need to think about it when testing by hand with curl.

### Tools available

Thirteen tools. Most are read-only; three write to the household (`mealmanager_save_recipe_draft`, `mealmanager_create_ingredient`, `mealmanager_add_inventory_item`). None accept `householdId` as input — it is always derived from the PAT.

| Tool | Purpose | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `mealmanager_list_inventory` | List current inventory items (id, ingredient name, category, quantity, location). | `{ location?: "pantry" \| "fridge" \| "freezer" }` |
| `mealmanager_list_recipes` | List household recipes (id, title, servings, updatedAt). | `{ query?: string }` (title substring) |
| `mealmanager_get_recipe` | Full recipe details with ingredient list. | `{ recipeId: string }` (UUID) |
| `mealmanager_get_menu_for_week` | Menu for a given week. Creates an empty menu if none exists (idempotent — matches the web behavior). | `{ weekStart: string }` (ISO date `YYYY-MM-DD` of a Monday) |
| `mealmanager_get_shopping_list` | Shopping list snapshot for a menu. | `{ menuId: string }` (UUID) |
| `mealmanager_list_ingredients` | Ingredients catalog (master list). | `{ query?: string, category?: string, storage?: "pantry"\|"fridge"\|"freezer", includeArchived?: boolean }` |
| `mealmanager_get_ingredient` | Full ingredient details with products attached. | `{ ingredientId: string }` (UUID) |
| `mealmanager_create_ingredient` | **Write.** Create an ingredient in the catalog (minimal fields; canonical unit locks once used). Returns the created ingredient incl. `id`. | `{ name: string, category: string, canonicalUnit: "g"\|"ml"\|"unit", storage: "pantry"\|"fridge"\|"freezer" }` |
| `mealmanager_add_inventory_item` | **Write.** Add/increment an inventory item (upsert by ingredient + location). Returns `{ item, created }`. | `{ ingredientId: string, quantity: { value, unit }, location?: "pantry"\|"fridge"\|"freezer" }` |
| `mealmanager_get_household` | Current household (id, name, members). | `{}` |
| `mealmanager_list_recipe_drafts` | List the household recipe drafts (id, title, source, updatedAt), newest first. | `{}` |
| `mealmanager_get_recipe_draft` | Full content of a recipe draft (free-text ingredients). | `{ draftId: string }` (UUID) |
| `mealmanager_save_recipe_draft` | **Write.** Persist a work-in-progress recipe draft for the household to review. `source` is forced to `mcp`. | `{ title?, instructions?, servings?, ingredients?: { name, quantity?: { value, unit }, raw? }[], sourceUrl? }` |

Each tool returns a single `text` content block containing the JSON-pretty-printed result of the underlying use case.

### Units

All quantities are stored in canonical units:
- Mass → `g` (grams)
- Volume → `ml` (millilitres)
- Discrete → `unit`

Conversions (kg ↔ g, L ↔ ml, cl ↔ ml, mg ↔ g) happen at the API boundary, not inside tool responses. The agent receives values in the canonical unit and can convert for display.

## Example: Claude Desktop config

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "meal-manager": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://your-domain.example/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer mm_pat_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Example: testing by hand with curl

List the available tools:

```bash
curl -X POST https://your-domain.example/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer mm_pat_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

Call a tool (here, list the inventory):

```bash
curl -X POST https://your-domain.example/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer mm_pat_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"mealmanager_list_inventory","arguments":{}}}'
```

The `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` header is mandatory — see "Required request headers" above.

## Example: Home Assistant (for voice via Google Nest / Gemini)

Today (May 2026) a Google Nest device cannot natively call third-party MCP servers. The pragmatic path for voice control is:

1. Install **Home Assistant** with the MCP client integration.
2. Add Meal Manager as an MCP server in HA (same URL + Bearer PAT as above).
3. Expose the resulting HA entities to Google Assistant via the official HA → Google Assistant integration.
4. "Hey Google, ask Home Assistant what's in the fridge" → HA proxies to Meal Manager via MCP.

Alternative: write a custom Gemini API client that uses MCP as a tool source.

## Architecture notes (for LLMs that read code)

- Hexagonal per bounded context under `server/contexts/<context>/{domain,application,infrastructure}`.
- The MCP transport layer is at `server/routes/mcp/`.
- The PAT domain lives in `server/contexts/platform/` alongside `User`.
- Hexagonal boundary rule: `domain` MUST NOT import frameworks. ESLint enforces this.

## Spec source

Read-only spec snapshots live under `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md`. The MCP integration was introduced by change `add-mcp-llm-integration`. Look at `openspec/changes/archive/` for archived proposals once shipped.

## Discovery endpoints

Four publicly-served resources let an agent or a scanner discover Meal Manager's capabilities without prior knowledge:

| Endpoint | Purpose | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `/robots.txt` | Bot Access Control — disallows AI crawlers from HTML pages. The legitimate agent channel is `/mcp` with a Bearer PAT. | `text/plain` |
| `/.well-known/api-catalog` | RFC 9727 API catalog — single entry point listing the available APIs (currently just `/mcp`) and pointing to their descriptions. | `application/linkset+json` |
| `/openapi-mcp.yaml` | OpenAPI 3.1 description of `/mcp` — declares the `bearerAuth` security scheme and the 13 `mealmanager_*` tools (each documented under the `x-mcp-tools` extension with its input schema). | `application/yaml` |
| `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` | Prose, human-readable guides for LLM operators. You are reading the latter. | `text/plain` |

In addition, every non-MCP HTTP response carries a `Link` header (RFC 8288) advertising these three resources, so a one-shot `HEAD /` lets an agent discover everything in a single round trip:

```
Link: </.well-known/api-catalog>; rel="api-catalog"; type="application/linkset+json",
      </llms.txt>; rel="llms-txt"; type="text/plain",
      </openapi-mcp.yaml>; rel="service-desc"; type="application/yaml"
```
